claims.text: Adding rare-earth elements to magnetic high-entropy alloys will increase the coercive field.
Rare-earth addition modifies the magnetic anisotropy of the alloy.
Modification of magnetic anisotropy is the mechanism by which rare-earth addition increases coercivity.
Rare-earth addition will produce a 10% increase in coercive field relative to the alloy without rare-earth elements.
The coercivity increase should occur in either the as-cast or annealed state.
The predicted effect should hold at room temperature under standard magnetic testing conditions.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on the identity of the rare-earth element.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on the rare-earth concentration.
The proposed experiment compares coercive field in an alloy with rare-earth addition against an alloy without rare-earth addition.
The hypothesis is falsified if the rare-earth-containing alloy does not have a coercive field at least 10% higher than the baseline.

contradictions.description: The outcome and falsification rule require an exact 10% increase, while the uncertainty field says the increase varies with rare-earth identity and concentration; no particular element or concentration is fixed to make the 10% threshold internally consistent.
